label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT - Monday casuals pay: briefing for Brian (read Sunday)

Brian,

This is what you need for Monday. Read it Sunday, keep it in your pocket on Monday. I'm sorry you're carrying this while I'm in the air. You shouldn't be the one facing this alone, but you're the right person for it, and the guys trust you.

WHAT HAPPENED

Friday's casual pay did not go out. On Thursday 27 November we sent the bank file for the fortnightly casual pay: 212 people. The bank had changed its file template on 25 November, and our file used the old one. The beneficiary reference field was too long, so the bank rejected the whole file before any payment was made. Nobody was paid twice, and nobody's money was lost. It just didn't move.

The rejection alert went to an old finance mailbox, so we only saw it after the bank cut-off had passed. That failure was ours, in finance and in the company. It was not the guys' fault. They did their work. Please say that plainly, and mean it. Don't go in defensive, and don't hint that the casuals should have checked anything.

WHEN THE MONEY LANDS

The fix is to pay through M-Pesa bulk instead of the bank. Management approved this on Friday morning. Kevin Mwangi in finance is running it.

Our target is 11am Monday for the money to be on phones. That is the only time you give. Do not promise earlier. Kevin has said the same. If you are asked for a specific time, say 11am is the target and that you will tell them personally as soon as there is a change, good or bad.

Mombasa 2024 is the reason for this rule. A supervisor told the casuals "by lunch," the money came at 4pm, and half the shift sat down. We are not doing that again. Never give a time we can't keep. If it is going to be later than 11, tell them as soon as you know, not after the deadline has passed.

WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE

1. The pay itself, on the M-Pesa batch, with the target of 11am Monday. The full amount on Peninah's list for each person.
2. Monday lunch and fare: KES 500 per head for every casual on the affected list, paid in the same M-Pesa batch.
3. The M-Pesa charges are paid by the company. Nobody's pay is reduced for them.
4. An apology from management, in person, from you. Njeri Wambua asked for this and approved it. Say it straight: "This was our mistake. We let you down. I'm sorry."
5. Peninah is at Embakasi from 7:30 with a printout of the list. Anyone who wants a payslip printed can ask her. She has the laptop.
6. If someone's number is wrong or missing, Peninah can fix it face to face. That is how the 14 people we couldn't reach will get paid.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT SAY OR PROMISE

1. Any time earlier than 11am for the money.
2. Any date or amount for the 14 unreachable people until Peninah has a working number for them. Don't guess.
3. Anything about contracts, dismissal, or threats. Procedure says no dismissal or threat of dismissal on the day, and I agree with it. Don't mention it even as a joke.
4. Anything about why the company is in this position beyond the plain fact: the bank rejected our file because of a format change, and we are paying through another route. Do not comment on company finances, cash, or whether money is tight. If asked, say the payment is approved and the route is set, and that you will get the answers for them.
5. Personal advances, loans, or rent money. Those are not approved. If someone asks, say you'll take it to HR and get back to them, then take it to HR.
6. Anything that links the money to the work. Don't say "no lunch unless you load." Lunch and fare are owed to them regardless.

OUMA

Ouma is loud, but he is not a bad man. He has four kids and rent due on the 1st, and he is speaking for people who are angry because they have been told "tomorrow" three times before. Treat him that way.

Talk to him first, privately, before you address the group. Joseph Kiprono, the shift supervisor, knows him and should be there. Ask what he needs to see to get his people moving. Acknowledge the rent. Don't argue about whose fault it is, and don't call him the ringleader in front of anyone.

Ask him to take the plan back to his group: the 11am target, the lunch and fare, Peninah at 7:30, and your apology. If he agrees, ask him to say it to the group himself. People listen to one of their own.

MONDAY TIMELINE

4:30am: I'm up. If anything changes overnight or early Monday, WhatsApp me before I board at 7:05. I will not have signal after that. If I'm not answering, go to Njeri Wambua.

5:30am: You're at the depot. Joseph is with you. Speak to Ouma privately first.

Before 6am: Get an HR person on site for the group conversation. The joint Ops and HR stoppage procedure requires it, and Peninah doesn't start until 7:30. Ask Njeri to name someone for 5:30 to 7:30. Don't go into the group without HR present.

About 6am: Talk to the whole group, with Joseph and the HR person beside you. Keep it short. Say what happened, what you're doing about it, the 11am target, the lunch and fare, and the apology. Then take questions.

7:30am: Peninah arrives. The 14 people without confirmed numbers can give her correct ones face to face.

Before 9am: The Kisumu trucks must leave by 9 or we lose the offloading slot at the mill. We cannot pay before 11, so do not promise loading by 9 as a reward for payment. If the trucks can't leave by 9, call the mill's offloading desk early and ask about moving the slot. Do this as soon as you know, not at 8:55.

11am: Target for the money on phones. Peninah and Kevin should confirm the batch has gone. Tell the group as soon as it's confirmed.

IF OUMA'S GROUP WON'T LOAD

Stay calm. Don't threaten, don't raise your voice, and don't bring in the police. Under the joint procedure, this is an Ops and HR matter, not a decision for you alone.

Ask what they need in order to start loading. Usually the answer is the 11am time and proof the money is moving. Show them Peninah's printout and the batch status once it exists.

Record who is refusing, by name, with the time. Ops and HR jointly keep that record. Do not write names on a whiteboard or announce them.

Nobody is dismissed or threatened with dismissal that day. If the stoppage continues after you have done all of the above, the decision on next steps is made by Ops and HR together, not by you at the depot.

Send me a WhatsApp update, and copy Njeri if it's serious. I'll read it as soon as I'm on the ground in Kampala, or sooner if I'm still in the air and it lands.

LAST THING

Say what you're going to do, then do it. Don't say anything you can't deliver. If you're not sure, say you're not sure and that you'll find out. The guys will forgive a late answer much faster than a broken promise.

Thanks for taking this, Brian. I know it's a lot to put on you in one weekend. I'm sorry it landed this way.

Achieng

reasons: The piece calls 27 November Thursday and says management approved M-Pesa on Friday morning, contrary to the stated dates.
